chunks: And through his chain of narration, from Al-Asamm, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom! Indeed, your father used to say regarding Hajj that for every Dirham he spent, a thousand Dirhams are recorded for him. So what is the reward for one who spends in traveling to your father, Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)? He said: O son of Sinan! For every Dirham, a thousand and a thousand are recorded for him — until he counted ten times. And his ranks are elevated by the same amount. And the pleasure of Allah is better for him, and the supplication of Muhammad (peace be upon him), and the supplication of the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams (peace be upon them) is better for him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material reward for spending money on visiting Imam Al-Husayn compared to Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam Al-Sadiq (a.s.) quantifies the spiritual merit of charity during the pilgrimage to Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.), stating that each Dirham spent yields a reward of ten thousand Dirhams, surpassing the standard Hajj reward. This multiplicative blessing is coupled with elevated ranks and the distinct advantage of the Imams' supplications, highlighting the unique status of Karbala as a locus of divine grace and intercession in Shia tradition.
